dedupe_keys.name: energy grid sizing toolbox wind nuclear and storage

description: The Energy Grid Sizing Toolbox is a small Windows program with a graphical interface for preliminary sizing of a grid that combines wind power, nuclear power and energy storage. It was published on Zenodo in October 2023 by Molly Ross, Nathan Chandra and Hitesh Bindra, with the full grid analysis in a paper in the MDPI journal Fluids. The user picks a storage technology (lithium-ion, lead-acid, thermal, pumped hydro or compressed air), a stochastic tuning parameter that sets how much wind fluctuation the nuclear plant follows, and the wind share of average load. It returns the required reactor size, storage size and utilisation, counts of large and small reactor power cycles over a year and the maximum ramp rate, and plots about 80 hours of nuclear, wind, storage and load. Coverage is not tied to a place. The tool is a Windows 7 or later executable with a README, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: no source code is published, and results are preliminary. Simulation uses are early-stage sizing of nuclear and storage to balance wind variability. Related records: model-system-advisor-model-sam gives more detailed plant performance modelling.
